text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.40% today to $151.41, capping a remarkable 10% surge over the past two weeks as oil prices have climbed sharply amid Middle East tensions. US crude has jumped to $107.89 per barrel, fueled by escalating threats to Saudi Arabian energy infrastructure from Iran-backed Houthi attacks and broader regional conflict; the company benefits directly as a major oil producer when crude prices rise this steeply. The stock's gains reflect investors rotating into energy plays that stand to profit from sustained geopolitical risk premiums baked into oil markets.

Today's modest daily move comes even as oil ticked slightly lower on reports of de-escalation talks between Saudi Arabia and Iran—a reminder that the underlying volatility remains high. The broader two-week rally shows the market is pricing in a durable shift in global energy dynamics away from Iran and toward U.S. producers and exporters, with deals like Qatar's US natural gas purchase signaling structural changes in where energy demand will flow.
